newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Jan-Mar industrial output down 15.4 perce.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Jan-Mar industrial output down 15.4 perce.

text.p: Bulgarian industrial output fell 15.4 percent in the first quarter of 1997 against the same period in 1996, the National Statistics Institute (NSI) said on Thursday.

"The industrial production fall in the first quarter of this year was due to the shrinking orders, reduced by soaring inflation and the sharp lev fall against the dollar, which curbed economic activity," an NSI official told a news conference.

Political instability and delayed reforms triggered first quarter cumulative consumer price inflation to 452 percent and March year-on-year inflation was 2,040.5 percent. Producer prices rose 2,072.7 percent year on year in March, the NSI figures showed.
The lev slumped to the record lows of 3,000-3,200 per dollar in February from around 500 at the start of the year.

Production of foods, drinks and tobbacco fell by 33 percent year on year. Oil processing declined by 22 percent. Machine building and electronics posted a fall of 26 percent in the first three months of this year.
State industrial sector's metal ore flotation posted a rise of 40 percent, metallurgy of 10 percent and chemical production of around three percent.
The private industrial sector share in total production was 18 percent. The production of the private sector fell six percent year-on-year.
"This was the first time when the private sector posted a fall in production, which began in February and continued in March," the NSI official added.
The fall was mainly due to the lower output of the private food and beverage industry, which was down around 30 percent year-on-year.
